title: Cornell officials pressed by faculty as outrage mounts over alleged gang rape | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Professors and staff at Cornell University grilled administration officials Tuesday as outrage builds over thealleged gang rape of a former studentat a fraternity house in 2024, with questions raised about how the school and law enforcement responded.

University officials confirmed two students named in a civil lawsuit filed last month by the woman are still enrolled and attending classes, according to a recording of a virtual webinar obtained by CNN.

Some faculty members said they are struggling to teach classes the accused students are in and raised questions about how to accommodate them and other students. They also pressed for answers about transparency and a perceived lack of communication over the case, and how to address cultural issues with Greek life on campus.

“This is certainly and most intimately a Cornell community cultural challenge that we’re facing,” Ryan Lombardi, vice president for student and campus life, said at the meeting. “But we know that the world is watching, and we know that we’re all feeling that.”

A spokesperson for Cornell University did not respond to CNN’s request for comment.

The meeting comes a day after faculty members submitted a resolution for a vote of no confidence against the school’s administrators.

Since the lawsuit was filed,frustrations on campushave grown with students and community members rallying in support of Jane Doe and calling for more accountability by university administrators.

A seven-hour sit-in is planned on campus Wednesday. The mayor of Ithaca, where Cornell is located, is also expected to hold a council meeting overhis proposal to pause Greek life and student gatherings.

University President Michael Kotlikoffreleased a videoover the weekend saying the school would take a “serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities on campus,” but cautioned Tuesday againsttargeting only Greek organizations.

“This is obviously an absolutely horrendous and inexcusable situation that occurred in a fraternity,” Kotlikoff said Tuesday. “But I have to make the point that this doesn’t only occur in fraternities, I worry about pushing this into the shadows, into houses which we don’t own, which are private houses, which have parties, and which things can occur beyond our purview.”

Help is available: For help in the US, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 or chat 24/7 ononline.rainn.org.

CNN’s Hanna Park, Kara Scannell, Taylor Galgano, Holly Yan and Isa Mudannayake contributed to this report.
